question: 不在一间屋里，还算一个团队吗？
question_en: Is it still a team if no one shares a room?
sub: 远程省下通勤、换来专注；信任、默会的手艺和走廊里的随口一问，却未必跟着搬进屏幕
sub_en: Remote work saves the commute and buys focus, but trust, tacit craft and the offhand hallway question don't necessarily follow people onto the screen

casting.reason: 他从『公司为什么存在』讲起：团队是为合同写不清的活而存在的，远程不消灭团队，只挪动边界——能写清的外包，写不清的才值得同处一室。
casting.reason_en: He starts from why firms exist at all: teams are there for the work no contract can spell out. Remote work doesn't abolish them; it moves the boundary, outsourcing what can be specified and keeping only what can't under one roof.

casting.reason: 他替远程辩护：办公室本就被『过度活跃的蜂巢思维』拖垮，团队靠的是流程而不是房间；后来也承认新人确实吃亏最多。
casting.reason_en: He defends remote work: the office was already wrecked by the hyperactive hive mind, and teams hold together through process, not rooms. He later concedes that newcomers really do lose the most.

casting.reason: 她把团队看成一个动作而非一个地点：能不能一起从错误里学，才决定团队算不算团队；远程的危险是沉默被当成同意。
casting.reason_en: She treats a team as something you do, not somewhere you are: whether it can learn from mistakes together is what makes it a team. The danger of remote work is that silence gets read as agreement.

casting.reason: 她用类比与比较学习的实验指出：办公室里的旁听是新人最大的并排比较样本库，远程砍掉它，吃亏最多的是刚入行的人。
casting.reason_en: Drawing on her experiments on analogy and comparison, she argues that overhearing colleagues is a newcomer's richest source of side-by-side cases; remote work cuts it off, and beginners pay the most.

casting.reason: 他把团队看成一个表演班子：视频会议几乎全是前台，远程团队缺的不是沟通次数，而是一块可以不装的后台。
casting.reason_en: He sees a team as a performance troupe: a video call is almost all front stage, and what remote teams lack isn't more communication but a backstage where no one has to act.

casting.reason: 他带来讲者与听者『脑际耦合』的实验：让大脑对齐的是共享的背景与来回反馈，而非共享的空气；远程损耗的是对话的节拍。
casting.reason_en: He brings experiments on speaker–listener brain coupling: what aligns brains is shared background and back-and-forth feedback, not shared air; what remote work wears down is the rhythm of conversation.

casting.reason: 他以轮扁斫轮说明手艺『口不能言』，又以『相濡以沫，不如相忘于江湖』反问：天天挤在一屋，未必是团队，倒可能是水快干了。
casting.reason_en: With the parable of Wheelwright Bian he shows that craft can't be put into words, and with the fish who 'wet one another with spit' he asks whether huddling in one room every day is a sign of a team or of water running out.

casting.reason: 他自己闻经于市井、受法于丈室：传法不须同院，却须入室——要紧的是有没有师徒全心相对的那一刻。
casting.reason_en: He was awakened by a stranger in the market and received the Dharma in his teacher's private room: transmission needn't happen in a shared courtyard, but it must happen in the inner room, in a moment when teacher and student face each other wholly.

posts.text: 先问一个更老的问题：公司为什么存在？市场上什么都能买，为何还要雇人坐在一起？因为有些活合同写不全——需求天天变，知识只此一家，每次重新谈判的交易成本太高，不如交给一段长期关系去随机应变。**团队是为合同写不清的那部分活而存在的。**远程本身不消灭团队，但会悄悄挪动边界：能写清的活外包出去，团队缩成一圈接单的承包商。问题不在屋子，在你的活有多少写不清。
posts.text_en: Start with an older question: why do firms exist at all? You can buy almost anything on the market, so why hire people and sit them together? Because some work can't be fully written into a contract: the requirements change daily, the know-how exists only here, and renegotiating every time carries transaction costs too high to bear, so you hand it to a long-term relationship that adapts as it goes. **A team exists for the part of the work no contract can spell out.** Remote work doesn't abolish teams, but it quietly moves the boundary: whatever can be specified gets outsourced, and the team shrinks into a ring of contractors taking orders. The question isn't the room. It's how much of your work can't be written down.

glossary.交易成本: transaction costs（交易成本）：做成一笔交易本身要付的代价——找人、谈价、立约、监督、扯皮。

glossary_en.transaction costs: The costs of doing a deal at all: finding a counterparty, bargaining, writing the contract, monitoring it and settling disputes.

posts.text: 我得替远程说句公道话：办公室从没保护过协作。开放式工位加上即时通讯，造出的是**过度活跃的蜂巢思维——人人随时被叫、随时回复，没人能连续想一小时。**很多团队远程后更累，是因为把走廊原样搬进了聊天窗口，几分钟就看一次消息。团队不靠房间凝聚，靠流程：任务写在公开看板上，谁负责什么一目了然；固定答疑时段，其余时间默认不打扰。这样的团队，隔着时区也成立。
posts.text_en: Let me put in a fair word for remote work: the office never protected collaboration. Open-plan desks plus instant messaging produced **the hyperactive hive mind: everyone summonable at any moment, answering at any moment, no one able to think for an hour straight.** Plenty of teams feel more drained after going remote because they moved the hallway, unchanged, into a chat window and now check messages every few minutes. Teams don't cohere through rooms; they cohere through process. Put tasks on a shared board so it's obvious who owns what; set fixed office hours for questions, and leave people alone the rest of the time by default. A team like that holds together across time zones.

glossary.过度活跃的蜂巢思维: hyperactive hive mind（过度活跃的蜂巢思维）：纽波特的用语，指靠随叫随到的消息往来推动工作、没有固定流程的协作方式。

glossary_en.hyperactive hive mind: Newport's term for a workflow driven by constant, unscheduled back-and-forth messaging instead of structured processes.

posts.text: 我研究医院和工厂里的团队二十多年，最能预测一个团队学得好不好的，不是成员多聪明，而是心理安全：大家敢不敢说『我不懂』『我搞砸了』。同处一屋时，这件事有很多隐形的帮手——会上皱一下眉，散会后有人追一句『你刚才是不是有顾虑』。视频会议把这些都滤掉了。**远程里的沉默看不见，只会被当成同意。**所以远程团队并非不能有心理安全，而是它不会自己长出来，得有人刻意去种。
posts.text_en: I've studied teams in hospitals and factories for more than twenty years. The best predictor of whether a team learns isn't how clever its members are but psychological safety: whether people dare to say 'I don't understand' or 'I messed up.' In a shared room this gets a lot of invisible help: a frown in the meeting, someone catching you afterwards with 'Did you have a concern back there?' Video calls filter all of that out. **On a remote team, silence is invisible, and it gets read as agreement.** So remote teams can have psychological safety, but it won't grow on its own. Someone has to plant it on purpose.

glossary.心理安全: psychological safety（心理安全）：团队成员共同相信，在这里提问、认错、提反对意见不会被羞辱或惩罚。

glossary_en.psychological safety: A shared belief among team members that it is safe to ask questions, admit mistakes or disagree without being humiliated or punished.

posts.text: 我关心的是新人怎么学会一门手艺。实验反复显示：只学一个案例，人几乎不会把它用到新问题上；把两个同构的案例并排比较，迁移率才大幅提高。办公室里，新人每天无意间旁听十几个『案例』——前辈怎么回难缠的客户、两人怎么为方案争、改稿前后差在哪——这是海量的、不用安排的并排比较。远程把这些旁听样本砍到接近零。老手损失不大，他们早有库存；**吃亏最多的是刚入行的人。**
posts.text_en: What I care about is how a newcomer learns a craft. Experiments show it again and again: learn from a single case and people almost never carry it over to a new problem; set two structurally matched cases side by side and compare them, and transfer jumps. In an office, a newcomer overhears a dozen 'cases' a day without trying: how a senior handles a difficult client, how two colleagues argue over a plan, what changed between the draft and the final version. That's an enormous stock of side-by-side comparisons nobody had to schedule. Remote work cuts those overheard samples to nearly zero. Veterans lose little; they already have their library. **The people who lose most are the ones just starting out.**

glossary.迁移: transfer（迁移）：把在一个情境里学到的方法，用到结构相同、外表不同的新问题上。

glossary_en.transfer: Applying a method learned in one situation to a new problem with the same structure but a different surface.

posts.text: 我看团队，看的是一个『表演班子』：成员一起在客户和上级面前维持一个印象，有人出错，别人立刻补台。表演要成立，必须有后台——茶水间里吐槽客户、排练说辞、卸下表情的地方。**视频会议几乎全是前台：每个人都在台上，还得一直看着自己的脸。**远程团队缺的不是沟通次数，是一块可以不装的地方。没有后台的班子，演得越久人越累，彼此也越像同台的陌生人。
posts.text_en: When I look at a team I see a performance team: its members jointly keep up an impression in front of clients and bosses, and when one of them slips, the others cover at once. For the show to work there has to be a backstage: the kitchen where you vent about the client, rehearse your lines and let your face go slack. **A video call is almost all front stage: everyone is on, and has to keep watching their own face.** What remote teams lack isn't the number of exchanges; it's a place where nobody has to put on an act. A troupe with no backstage gets more tired the longer it plays, and its members come to feel like strangers sharing a stage.

glossary.后台: backstage（后台）：戈夫曼拟剧论的用语，指不面对观众、可以放下表演、为前台做准备的区域，与『前台』相对。

glossary_en.backstage: In Goffman's dramaturgical sociology, the region out of the audience's sight where performers drop the act and prepare for the front stage.

posts.text: 我在扫描仪里测过讲者和听者的大脑：一个人讲故事，听者的脑活动会跟着讲者同步起伏，听懂得越多，同步越强，理解最好的人甚至会提前一步。有意思的是，这种耦合用录音也能出现，不需要同在一屋。真正让大脑对齐的，是共享的上下文和一来一回的反馈。麻烦在视频的延迟：对话里轮流说话的间隙通常只有约 200 毫秒，卡顿会打乱这个节拍。**远程损耗的是节拍，不是空气。**
posts.text_en: I've put speakers and listeners in the scanner. When someone tells a story, the listener's brain activity rises and falls in step with the speaker's; the more the listener understands, the stronger the synchrony, and the best comprehenders even run slightly ahead. Interestingly, this coupling shows up with a recording too. It doesn't need a shared room. What actually aligns brains is shared context and feedback going back and forth. The trouble with video is lag: the gap between turns in conversation is usually around 200 milliseconds, and a stutter in the connection throws that beat off. **What remote work wears down is the rhythm, not the air.**

glossary.耦合: neural coupling（耦合）：两个大脑的活动在时间上相互对应、此起彼伏，这里指听者的脑活动追随讲者。

glossary_en.coupling: Activity in two brains corresponding over time; here, the listener's brain tracking the speaker's.

posts.text: 桓公读书于堂上，轮扁斫轮于堂下，曰：『君之所读者，古人之糟粕已夫！』斫轮，徐则甘而不固，疾则苦而不入，**不徐不疾，得之于手而应于心，口不能言。**臣不能以喻臣之子，臣之子亦不能受之于臣，是以行年七十而老斫轮。今人以文书影像传艺，皆糟粕也。然轮扁父子同处一室数十年，其子亦不能受——屋何与焉？
posts.text_en: Duke Huan was reading in the hall above; Wheelwright Bian was cutting a wheel below. He said, 'What my lord is reading is nothing but the dregs of the ancients!' When you cut a wheel, go too slowly and the joint is loose and won't hold; go too fast and it binds and won't go in. **Neither too slow nor too fast: you get it in the hand and it answers in the heart, but the mouth cannot put it into words.** I can't explain it to my son, and my son can't receive it from me, so here I am at seventy, still cutting wheels. People today pass on craft through documents and videos: dregs, all of it. And yet Bian and his son shared a workshop for decades and the son still couldn't receive it. So what has the room got to do with it?
posts.vernacular: 齐桓公在堂上读书，造车轮的轮扁在堂下干活，说：『您读的不过是古人留下的糟粕罢了！』削车轮，下手慢了就松滑不牢，快了就紧涩装不进，**不快不慢，手上找到了分寸、心里自然应和，嘴上却说不出来。**我没法讲给儿子明白，儿子也没法从我这里学去，所以我七十岁了还在亲手削车轮。如今的人靠文档、视频传手艺，也都是糟粕。可轮扁父子同在一间屋里几十年，儿子还是学不会——这跟屋子有什么关系？

glossary.轮扁: Wheelwright Bian（轮扁）：《庄子·天道》寓言里造车轮的匠人，名扁。
glossary.糟粕: dregs（糟粕）：酿酒剩下的渣子，比喻失去精华的残余。

glossary_en.Wheelwright Bian: A wheelwright in a parable from the Zhuangzi ('The Way of Heaven') who tells a duke that books hold only the dregs of the ancients.

posts.text: 吾本不识字，卖柴于市，闻一客诵《金刚经》，心即开悟。彼客非吾师，亦非同屋之人。后至黄梅，五祖以杖击碓三下，吾会其意，三鼓入室，祖以袈裟遮围，为说《金刚经》，至『应无所住而生其心』，言下大悟。**是知传法不须同院，却须入室。**汝等争屋与非屋，皆住于相。要问者：可曾有一刻，师徒全心相对？
posts.text_en: I could not read. I was selling firewood in the market when I heard a customer reciting the Diamond Sutra, and my mind opened at once. That man was not my teacher, nor did we share a roof. Later, at Huangmei, the Fifth Patriarch struck the rice mortar three times with his staff; I took his meaning, and at the third watch of the night I entered his room. He screened us with his robe and expounded the Diamond Sutra to me, and at the line 'let the mind arise without dwelling on anything' I was fully awakened. **So the Dharma need not be passed on in a shared courtyard, but it must be passed on in the inner room.** You argue over room or no room, and all of you are clinging to forms. The question is: has there ever been a moment when teacher and student faced each other with their whole minds?
posts.vernacular: 我本来不识字，在集市上卖柴，听见一位客人诵《金刚经》，心里当下就开悟了。那客人不是我的老师，也不是同住一屋的人。后来我到黄梅，五祖用手杖在舂米的碓上敲了三下，我领会了他的意思，三更时进了他的房间，五祖用袈裟围住遮挡，给我讲《金刚经》，讲到『应无所住而生其心』，我当下彻悟。**可见传法不必天天同住一个院子，但一定要有『入室』的那一刻。**你们争论在不在一间屋，都是执着于外相。该问的是：师徒之间，可曾有过一刻全心全意地面对面？

glossary.入室: entering the room（入室）：禅门用语，弟子进入师父丈室单独受教，引申为得到亲传。
glossary.住于相: clinging to forms（住于相）：佛教语，执着于事物的外在形相而看不到本质。

glossary_en.inner room: In Chan usage, the master's private chamber, where a disciple receives teaching one to one; by extension, direct personal transmission.
glossary_en.clinging to forms: A Buddhist phrase for fixating on the outward appearance of things and missing their nature.

posts.text: @根特纳 旁听样本是真的，但办公室也在淹没它：新人坐在开放工位，一天被打断几十次，听到的多半是噪音，不是案例。**学徒制不该寄托在偶然听见上，应该刻意设计。**讨论放在公开频道而不是私聊里，新人随时能翻；每周两次结对干活，屏幕共享、边做边讲；资深的人把『我为什么这么改』写成三行备注。把偶然撞上的学习，换成可以检索的学习。
posts.text_en: @Gentner The overheard samples are real, but the office drowns them too: a newcomer at an open-plan desk gets interrupted dozens of times a day, and most of what they hear is noise, not cases. **Apprenticeship shouldn't hinge on happening to overhear things; it should be designed.** Keep discussions in public channels rather than private messages, so newcomers can scroll back any time; pair up twice a week, screen shared, talking as you work; have seniors jot three lines on 'why I changed it this way.' Swap learning you stumble into for learning you can search.

glossary.结对: pairing（结对）：两人共用一个屏幕，一人操作、一人旁看并随时讨论的协作方式，源自结对编程。

glossary_en.pair up: To work as two on one screen, one driving and one watching and discussing as you go, a practice borrowed from pair programming.

posts.text: @纽波特 刻意设计很好，但要小心：刻意挑出来给新人看的，往往是整理过的好例子。**比较最需要的是对照——失败的、做到一半的、两个人做法不同的。**公开频道里只剩结论，过程和弯路都在私下消化了。我的建议是让对照成为惯例：每次复盘同时摆出两个方案，一个成了、一个砸了，让新人自己说出差在哪。说得出差异，才算学到了结构。
posts.text_en: @Newport Designing it is fine, but watch out: what gets hand-picked for newcomers tends to be the tidy, good examples. **What comparison needs most is contrast: the failures, the half-finished, two people doing it differently.** A public channel ends up holding only conclusions; the process and the detours get digested in private. My suggestion is to make contrast routine: at every post-mortem, lay out two approaches side by side, one that worked and one that flopped, and let the newcomer say where they differ. Being able to name the difference is what it means to have learned the structure.

glossary.复盘: post-mortem（复盘）：事后把做事的过程重新摆一遍，找出哪里做对、哪里做错。

glossary_en.post-mortem: A review held after a project or incident to reconstruct what happened and why.

posts.text: @纽波特 你的流程对能拆成模块的活管用——写进看板的，本质上就是一份小合同。可合同永远写不全，写不全的那部分，过去靠一屋子人之间的关系和权威随手兜住。还有一笔账没人提：有研究发现，工程师坐得离队友近，新人得到的反馈明显更多，代价是老手自己的产出下降。**远程没有消灭培养新人的成本，只是没人再愿意付。**结果是公司只招熟手。
posts.text_en: @Newport Your process works for work that breaks into modules: anything you can put on a board is, at bottom, a small contract. But contracts are never complete, and the incomplete part used to be caught on the fly by the relationships and authority among people in one room. There's also a bill nobody mentions: research has found that when engineers sit near their teammates, the juniors get markedly more feedback, at the cost of the seniors' own output. **Remote work didn't eliminate the cost of training newcomers; it just left no one willing to pay it.** The upshot is that companies hire only the experienced.

posts.text: @威廉姆森 你把团队讲成合同加权威，可我研究过很多从不共处一室的团队：手术室里临时凑起的组、跨三个时区的项目组，还有 2010 年智利矿难救援——各国工程师、矿企和政府人员临时拼成一支队伍。我管这叫 teaming：团队是一个动作，不是一个地点。**判断一个团队算不算团队，看它能不能一起从错误里学。**这可以远程练：复盘时领导先讲自己错在哪。
posts.text_en: @Williamson You describe a team as contracts plus authority, but I've studied plenty of teams that never shared a room: surgical crews thrown together for one operation, project groups spanning three time zones, the 2010 Chilean mine rescue, where engineers, a mining company and government officials from several countries improvised a single team. I call it teaming: a team is something you do, not somewhere you are. **Whether a team counts as a team depends on whether it can learn from its mistakes together.** That can be practised remotely: at the post-mortem, the leader names their own mistake first.

glossary.teaming: teaming（组队协作）：埃德蒙森的概念，指人们为某项任务临时组合、边做边协作，而不依赖固定的成员和地点。

glossary_en.teaming: Edmondson's term for people coming together around a task and coordinating on the fly, without relying on fixed membership or a fixed place.

posts.text: @哈森 你测到的同步，来自听一个讲好的故事。可真实的会议里人人都在表演：点头、附和、说『好的没问题』。**台前的同步，可能只是一场演得整齐的戏。**真正的分歧、担心和怨气，都在后台才说出口。远程团队把后台砍掉，前台就只剩整齐。所以别只问开了多少会，要问有没有一个不用开摄像头、没有议程、说错话也不会被记下来的地方。
posts.text_en: @Hasson The synchrony you measured comes from listening to a well-told story. In a real meeting everyone is performing: nodding, agreeing, saying 'Sure, no problem.' **Synchrony on the front stage may be nothing more than a well-drilled show.** The real disagreements, worries and grudges only come out backstage. Cut the backstage, as remote teams do, and all that's left on the front stage is tidiness. So don't just ask how many meetings you hold; ask whether there's a place with no camera and no agenda, where a careless remark won't end up on the record.

posts.text: @戈夫曼 说得对，同步不等于理解。我们做过一个实验：同一段故事，先给两组人不同的背景信息，他们对故事的解读分道扬镳，**大脑活动也跟着分开——对齐的是解读，不是字句。**这恰好说明后台的价值：茶水间闲聊不是浪费，它在悄悄积累共享背景。远程团队可以补：开会先用三分钟对齐『我们为什么做这件事』；难谈的事改用语音而不是打字，语气里带着一半信息。
posts.text_en: @Goffman You're right that synchrony isn't understanding. We ran an experiment: give two groups different background before the same story, and their readings of it part ways, **and so does their brain activity: what aligns is the interpretation, not the words.** Which is exactly why the backstage matters. Kitchen chatter isn't wasted time; it quietly builds up shared background. Remote teams can make up for it: open each meeting with three minutes on why we're doing this at all, and take difficult conversations to voice instead of typing, since tone carries half the message.

posts.text: 泉涸，鱼相与处于陆，相呴以湿，相濡以沫，不如相忘于江湖。**鱼相忘乎江湖，人相忘乎道术。**威廉姆森言团队存乎契约之不能尽，是也；然必日日同屋、相呴相濡，乃水之将涸也。庖丁解牛，依乎天理，未尝日问于文惠君。各得其水，各尽其技，虽千里亦一队；无水而强聚，同屋亦涸辙之鱼耳。
posts.text_en: When the spring dries up, the fish are stranded together on dry land; they moisten one another with their breath and wet one another with spit. Better that they forget one another in the rivers and lakes. **Fish forget one another in the rivers and lakes; people forget one another in the arts of the Way.** Williamson says a team exists for what contracts can't cover, and he's right. But if people must huddle in one room every day, breathing on one another, that is a sign the water is running out. Cook Ding carved the ox along its natural seams and never had to check in with Lord Wenhui every day. When each has their own water and uses their full skill, a team holds together a thousand li apart; force people together with no water and, room or no room, they're fish in a dried-up rut.
posts.vernacular: 泉水干了，鱼一起困在陆地上，互相吐湿气、互相用唾沫沾湿，不如在江湖里彼此忘掉。**鱼在江湖里相忘，人在大道里相忘。**威廉姆森说团队是为合同写不尽的部分而存在，说得对；可要是非得天天挤在一屋、互相吐沫取暖，那正是水快干了的样子。庖丁解牛，顺着牛身天然的纹理下刀，从不需要天天去请示文惠君。各自得了自己的水、使尽自己的本事，相隔千里也是一支队伍；没有水却硬凑在一起，同在一屋也不过是车辙里快干死的鱼。

glossary.相濡以沫: moistening each other with spit（相濡以沫）：《庄子·大宗师》语，困在干涸处的鱼互吐唾沫相润，比喻困境中勉强相救。
glossary.庖丁: Cook Ding（庖丁）：《庄子·养生主》里的厨师，解牛十九年刀刃如新，喻顺应自然之理而技近于道。
glossary.涸辙之鱼: fish in a dried-up rut（涸辙之鱼）：困在将干的车辙积水里的鱼，比喻处境窘迫。

glossary_en.Cook Ding: The cook in the Zhuangzi ('The Secret of Caring for Life') whose blade stays sharp for nineteen years because he cuts along the ox's natural seams; an image of skill that has become the Way.
glossary_en.li: A traditional Chinese unit of distance, roughly half a kilometre.

posts.text: 庄子道轮扁之子不能受，然何以不能受？非屋之过，是子不自斫也。吾在五祖处，踏碓八月余，未敢行至堂前，及至入室，一言即悟。**迷时师度，悟了自度。**师可指路，路须自行。今之新人隔屏学艺，师若只授文书，是授糟粕；徒若只看不做，同屋亦枉然。须令其自斫一轮，斫坏了，师于旁一言点破。
posts.text_en: Zhuangzi says the wheelwright's son couldn't receive it. But why couldn't he? Not because of the room. Because the son never cut a wheel himself. At the Fifth Patriarch's monastery I spent more than eight months treading the rice pestle out back, never daring to approach the Dharma hall; then, on the night I entered his room, a single line awakened me. **When deluded, the teacher ferries you across; once awakened, you ferry yourself.** A teacher can point the way; the walking is yours. Newcomers today learn their craft through a screen. If the master hands over only documents, he hands over dregs; if the apprentice only watches and never does, sharing a room is no help. Have him cut a wheel himself, and when he ruins it, the master standing by puts it right in a single word.
posts.vernacular: 庄子说轮扁的儿子学不会，可他为什么学不会？不是屋子的问题，是儿子没自己动手去削。我在五祖那里，在后院踩碓舂米八个多月，从不敢走到法堂前，等到入室那一夜，一句话就开悟了。**迷的时候靠师父度，悟了之后要自己度。**师父可以指路，路得自己走。如今的新人隔着屏幕学手艺，师父要是只给文档，给的就是糟粕；徒弟要是只看不做，同在一屋也白搭。得让他自己削一个轮子，削坏了，师父在旁边一句话点破。

glossary.碓: rice pestle（碓）：舂米的器具，用脚踏动木杵起落。
glossary.度: ferry across（度）：佛教语，原指渡人过河，喻引导人脱离迷惑。

glossary_en.ferries you across: A Buddhist image: the teacher as a boatman carrying the deluded over the river of confusion.

posts.text: 听下来，大家其实同意一件事：团队不是一个坐标，是一套共同维持的东西——用我的话说是一个班子，用埃德蒙森的话说是一起学习。屋子只是最省事的维持方式，远程团队得自己补上屋子顺手给的那些。我的建议：**给团队留一块后台**——一个没有领导、不留记录的闲聊群；一周一次不开摄像头的电话，只聊近况；允许开会时关掉自己的画面，别逼人一直盯着自己的脸演戏。演累了的人，不会说真话。
posts.text_en: Listening to all this, we actually agree on one thing: a team isn't a set of coordinates but something people keep up together, a troupe in my terms, learning together in Edmondson's. The room was just the cheapest way to keep it up, and remote teams have to supply for themselves what the room used to hand out in passing. My advice: **give the team a backstage.** A chat group with no boss in it and no record kept; a weekly call with cameras off, just to catch up; permission to switch off your own video in meetings, so no one has to perform while staring at their own face. People worn out from performing don't tell the truth.

posts.text: 我的结论：远程也能让大脑对齐，但对齐靠共享的背景和来回的反馈，这两样在屋里是顺带产生的，远程得专门制造。**难的事说出声，简单的事写下来。**分歧、批评、坏消息，用语音或视频，别用文字——没有语气的文字最容易被读成敌意。重要的事讲成一个有前因后果的故事，而不是一张清单。再有，定期见面不是奢侈，是给共享背景充电：一个季度聚上两天，未必比天天通勤差。
posts.text_en: My conclusion: remote work can still align brains, but alignment rests on shared background and back-and-forth feedback, which a room produces as a by-product and remote work has to manufacture on purpose. **Say hard things out loud; write easy things down.** Disagreement, criticism and bad news belong on voice or video, not text: toneless text is the easiest thing in the world to read as hostility. Explain important things as a story with causes and consequences, not as a list. And meeting in person now and then isn't a luxury; it recharges the shared background. Two days together every quarter may do as much as commuting every day.

posts.text: 我同意纽波特，学习不能靠偶然；也同意慧能，只看不做学不到结构。合起来是一条能走的路。如果你是新人：**每周找两个同类的案例并排看，逼自己写下它们哪里一样、哪里不一样**——两封客户邮件、两版方案、两次复盘都行；请前辈给你看废稿，不只是定稿。如果你带新人：讲一次成功，就配一次失败；入职头三个月多安排同处一室的日子，那是他们样本最缺的时候。
posts.text_en: I agree with Newport that learning can't be left to chance, and with Huineng that watching without doing never yields the structure. Put together, that's a path you can walk. If you're new: **each week, find two cases of the same kind, look at them side by side, and make yourself write down where they match and where they differ.** Two client emails, two versions of a plan, two post-mortems will all do; and ask seniors to show you their discarded drafts, not just the final ones. If you're training someone: for every success you walk through, pair it with a failure; and in the first three months, schedule more days in the same room, because that's when their stock of cases is thinnest.

posts.text: 我的结论是：在不在一屋，不决定团队算不算团队；能不能一起把错误说出口，才决定。屋子只是降低了开口的门槛，远程要靠带队的人刻意把门槛压低。三件事今天就能做：**开会最后点名问一个人『你有什么顾虑』**，而不是笼统地问『大家有问题吗』；复盘时你先讲自己哪里判断错了；有人报坏消息时，你的第一句话是谢谢。做到这三件，隔着时区也会有人敢开口。
posts.text_en: My conclusion: whether people share a room doesn't decide whether they're a team; whether they can say their mistakes out loud together does. The room only lowered the threshold for speaking up, and remote teams need whoever leads them to lower it on purpose. Three things you can do today: **end each meeting by asking one person, by name, 'What concerns do you have?'** rather than a vague 'Any questions?'; at the post-mortem, say first where your own judgment went wrong; and when someone brings bad news, make your first words 'thank you.' Do those three, and people will speak up even across time zones.

posts.text: 我收回一半：威廉姆森和根特纳说服了我，新人确实在远程中吃亏最多。但解法不是回到开放工位的蜂巢，而是让协作有个形状。**默认异步，同步是例外而不是常态。**每天给自己留两段不看消息的整块时间；团队定好固定答疑时段，其余时间的问题写进公开文档；每周一次结对干活，专门留给新人。别把走廊搬进聊天窗口——那样你既没得到专注，也没得到走廊。
posts.text_en: I'll take back half of what I said: Williamson and Gentner have convinced me that newcomers really do lose the most when work goes remote. But the fix isn't a return to the open-plan hive; it's giving collaboration a shape. **Default to asynchronous; make real-time the exception, not the norm.** Keep two blocks a day for yourself with no messages; have the team set fixed office hours, and put questions that come up the rest of the time into a shared document; reserve one paired session a week for newcomers. Don't move the hallway into a chat window: do that and you get neither focus nor a hallway.

posts.text: 把账算清楚就好办了。先给手上的活分类：能写清交付标准的，远程甚至外包都行；写不清、靠默会知识、要随时临场调整的，值得付同处一室的成本。**问题从来不是远程还是坐班，而是哪部分活该放在哪。**对公司：把带新人的成本写进预算，别让老手私下吃亏。对个人：刚入行时，优先选能坐在熟手旁边的岗位，或者入职时就把『谁带我、多久一次』谈清楚——这是职业早期最值钱的一条。
posts.text_en: Once the accounts are clear, the rest is manageable. Start by sorting your work: whatever has a clearly specifiable deliverable can be done remotely, even outsourced; whatever can't be written down, depends on tacit knowledge and needs adjusting on the spot is worth paying the cost of sharing a room. **The question was never remote versus office; it's which part of the work belongs where.** For companies: put the cost of training newcomers into the budget, so seniors aren't quietly absorbing it. For individuals: early in your career, favour jobs where you sit next to someone experienced, or settle at the start who will mentor you and how often. That's the most valuable term you'll negotiate early on.

glossary.默会知识: tacit knowledge（默会知识）：会做却说不清的知识，如手感、分寸、判断力，难以写成文档传递。

glossary_en.tacit knowledge: Know-how a person can exercise but cannot fully articulate, such as feel, timing or judgment; hard to pass on in documents.

posts.text: 诸君所言，归于一处：传在人，不在屋。然人亦可日日相对，而心不相对。吾劝诸君：不必日日同院，**每月须有一回入室**——师徒放下事务，全心对坐一个时辰，徒问其所惑，师点其所迷。平日则各自斫轮，各自踏碓。心若相对，千里亦是同室；心不相对，同室亦隔千里。
posts.text_en: What you have all said comes to one thing: transmission lies in people, not in rooms. Yet people can face each other every day while their minds never meet. My counsel: you need not share a courtyard every day, **but once a month there must be an entering of the room.** Teacher and student set their tasks aside and sit facing each other, wholly present, for an hour or two; the student asks what puzzles him, the teacher points out where he is stuck. The rest of the time, each cuts his own wheel and treads his own pestle. When minds meet, a thousand li is the same room; when they don't, the same room is a thousand li apart.
posts.vernacular: 各位所说的，归结到一处：传承在人，不在屋子。但人也可能天天面对面，心却不在一处。我劝各位：不必天天同在一个院子，**但每个月要有一次『入室』**——师父和徒弟放下手头的事，全心全意对坐一两个小时，徒弟问他困惑的，师父点破他卡住的。平时就各自削轮子、各自踩碓干活。心若相对，相隔千里也像同在一屋；心不相对，同在一屋也像隔着千里。

posts.text: 屋与非屋，犹蝶与周，何必辨之？吾所虑者，不在相隔，在相缚。日日会、时时报，如鱼处陆，相濡以沫，疲而不觉。**与其多会，不如同作一事。**轮扁之艺，口不能言，然可同斫一轮。诸君：少开一会，多同作一器；功成之后，相忘可也。
posts.text_en: Room or no room: it's like the butterfly and Zhou, so why insist on telling them apart? What worries me isn't distance but bondage. Meetings every day, reports every hour: fish on dry land, wetting one another with spit, too tired to notice. **Rather than meeting more, make one thing together.** Wheelwright Bian's craft can't be put into words, but two people can cut one wheel together. So: skip one meeting, and build one thing side by side; once it's done, you're free to forget one another.
posts.vernacular: 在屋里还是不在屋里，就像蝴蝶和庄周，何必分得那么清？我担心的不是彼此相隔，而是彼此捆绑。天天开会、时时汇报，就像鱼困在陆上，互相吐沫，累了也不自知。**与其多开会，不如一起做成一件事。**轮扁的手艺说不出来，却可以两人一起削一个轮子。各位：少开一个会，多一起做一件东西；事情做成了，彼此忘掉也无妨。

glossary.蝶与周: the butterfly and Zhou（蝶与周）：庄周梦蝶，醒来不知是庄周梦见蝴蝶，还是蝴蝶梦见庄周，喻物我界限本不必分明。

glossary_en.the butterfly and Zhou: From Zhuangzi's dream: waking, he could not tell whether Zhou had dreamed he was a butterfly or a butterfly was dreaming it was Zhou; an image of boundaries that need not be fixed.

summaries.summary: 全场最大的共识是：**团队不是一个地点，而是一套需要持续维护的东西**——共享的背景、敢开口的氛围、新人看得见的样本、一起动手的时刻。屋子曾把这些顺手送上，远程就得专门去造。分歧在于造不造得出来：纽波特和埃德蒙森认为流程与习惯能补上大半；威廉姆森、根特纳提醒，默会的手艺和带新人的成本最难补，吃亏的是新人；庄子与慧能则把问题从『屋』移到『心』，要紧的是有没有一起做事、全心相对的时刻。
summaries.summary_en: The broadest agreement is that **a team isn't a place but something that has to be kept up**: shared background, a climate where people dare to speak, cases a newcomer can actually see, moments of working on something together. The room used to supply these in passing; remote teams have to build them deliberately. The disagreement is over whether they can be built. Newport and Edmondson think process and habit can make up most of the gap. Williamson and Gentner warn that tacit craft and the cost of training newcomers are the hardest parts to replace, and that beginners bear the loss. Zhuangzi and Huineng move the question from the room to the mind: what matters is whether there are moments of making something together and facing one another with full attention.
summaries.insight: 十七、十八世纪的欧洲学者早就在远程协作：『书信共和国』里，人们隔着国境靠信件讨论、互审、合写，一封信常常要在路上走好几周。它能运转，靠的不是频繁，而是**每一封都写得完整**——前因、推理、疑问都摆清楚，读的人不用追问就能接着往下做。今天的远程协作恰好反过来：消息又短又碎，随发随问，把异步用成了慢一拍的同步。与其追求回得更快，不如学着把一条消息写成一封信：写的人多花十分钟，读的人省下一来一回。
summaries.insight_en: European scholars of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries were already collaborating remotely: in the Republic of Letters, people argued, reviewed each other's work and wrote together across borders by post, with a single letter often spending weeks on the road. It worked not because exchanges were frequent but because **each letter was written to be complete**: background, reasoning and open questions all laid out, so the reader could carry on without having to ask. Remote work today does the opposite. Messages are short and fragmented, fired off and followed by questions, turning asynchronous work into synchronous work running a beat behind. Rather than trying to reply faster, learn to write a message as a letter: the writer spends ten more minutes, and the reader is spared a round trip.
summaries.advice: 1）本周把手上的活分成两栏：写得清交付标准的，和写不清、靠手感的；后者别全靠文档和视频，去争取和熟手同处、一起动手的时间。2）下次开会结束前，点名问一个人『你有什么顾虑』，复盘时先讲自己的错。3）如果你是新人，每周找两个同类案例并排比较、写下异同，再请前辈给你看一份废稿。4）下一条发给同事的长消息，照一封信来写：背景、你的判断、要对方做什么，**一次说完，让读的人不用追问**。
summaries.advice_en: 1) This week, split your work into two columns: things with a clearly specifiable deliverable, and things that can't be written down and run on feel. For the second column, don't rely on documents and videos alone; push for time working alongside someone experienced. 2) Before your next meeting ends, ask one person by name, 'What concerns do you have?', and at the next post-mortem name your own mistake first. 3) If you're new, compare two cases of the same kind side by side each week, write down how they match and differ, and ask a senior to show you one of their discarded drafts. 4) Write your next long message to a colleague as a letter: the background, your judgment, what you need from them. **Say it all at once, so the reader doesn't have to ask.**

summaries.summary: 团队并不由共同地址定义，而由共同目标、相互依赖，以及能否一起暴露问题、修正错误来定义。圆桌大体同意，办公室会顺带提供共享背景、非正式后台、默会学习和新人反馈；远程并非做不到，只是必须显性设计并付费。**真正的分歧不在“远程能否成队”，而在什么工作、什么阶段值得购买同处一室的高带宽。**异步流程能保护专注，却难完全替代含混任务中的临场调整、心理安全和学徒观察。因此稳妥答案不是选边，而是按任务含混度、人员资历与关系成熟度安排协作方式。
summaries.insight: 混合办公里最危险的往往不是距离，而是距离不对称：有人天天同屋，有人长期在线。前者会在会前、会后和午餐时先形成判断，后者只看到已经包装好的正式决定；久而久之，信息、发言权与晋升机会都会向可见者集中。这比全员远程更难治理，因为组织容易误以为接入视频就等于平等参与。**只要关键决定仍在房间里发生，远程成员就不是同等队员，而只是被通知的人。**选择混合岗位时，别只问每周到岗几天，还要问领导在哪里、决策在哪里发生，以及远程同事能否带项目和晋升。
summaries.advice: 本周先做三件事。第一，把未来两周任务分成“标准清楚”“需要探索”“需要带教”三类：第一类异步推进，后两类预订同步共创或见面时间。第二，定一份轻量沟通约定：消息默认多久回复、坏消息走语音、决定写入同一份日志，并给每人两段免打扰时间。第三，若是混合团队，实行“一人远程，全员同屏”，会前发材料，会后记录异议、负责人和复查日期；同时把新人结对时数计入老手工作量。**别用更多会议补距离，要用清楚的规则、受保护的带教和公平的决策入口补距离。**
summaries.summary_en: A team is defined less by a shared address than by common goals, mutual dependence, and the ability to surface problems and learn together. The broad agreement here is that offices provide shared context, informal backstage space, tacit learning, and feedback almost incidentally. Remote teams can create the same functions, but only through deliberate design and real investment. **The central disagreement is not whether remote teams can be real teams, but which work and career stages justify paying for the higher bandwidth of being together.** Asynchronous systems protect concentration, yet they cannot fully replace live adjustment, psychological safety, or apprenticeship when work is ambiguous. The practical answer is therefore contingent: choose the collaboration mode according to task ambiguity, experience level, and how mature the working relationships are.
summaries.insight_en: The biggest danger in hybrid work is often not distance itself but unequal distance: some people share a room every day while others remain permanently online. Those in the room form opinions before meetings, refine them afterward, and exchange context over lunch. Remote colleagues receive the polished decision rather than participating in its formation. Over time, information, influence, and promotion opportunities drift toward whoever is physically visible. This can be harder to govern than a fully remote setup because joining by video creates an illusion of equal access. **If consequential decisions still happen in the room, remote employees are not equal teammates; they are people who get notified.** When considering a hybrid role, ask not only how many office days are required, but where leaders work, where decisions happen, and whether remote employees actually lead projects and earn promotions.
summaries.advice_en: Take three steps this week. First, sort the next two weeks of work into three buckets: clearly specified, exploratory, and apprenticeship-heavy. Handle the first asynchronously; reserve live collaboration or in-person time for the other two. Second, create a lightweight communication agreement covering expected response times, when bad news should move to voice, where decisions are logged, and which daily blocks are protected from interruption. Third, in a hybrid team, use the rule “if one person is remote, everyone joins on their own screen.” Circulate materials beforehand, then record objections, owners, and review dates afterward. Count mentoring hours as part of senior employees’ workload rather than invisible generosity. **Do not compensate for distance with more meetings; compensate with clearer rules, protected teaching time, and equal access to decisions.**

summaries.summary: 物理房间从不自动生成团队，它只是把信任、共享背景、旁听学艺和心理安全当作“免费副产品”顺手送给了同屋的人。离开房间后，团队并未瓦解，**但过去靠空气顺带完成的一切，现在都必须被刻意设计和买单，尤其是培养新人这笔隐形账。**真正的分歧在于怎么重建：纽波特主张用异步规则和公开看板对抗噪音；埃德蒙森、戈夫曼与哈森则认为流程不够，必须补上敢认错的安全感、不装的“后台”和带语气的声音；庄子与慧能更彻底，直接质疑“高频沟通”本身——与其日日开会相濡以沫，不如各自专注手艺，关键处同做一器、全心相对。
summaries.insight: 在办公室里说句蠢话、叹口气，声波散进空气就消失了；而在远程软件里，每一句发言、每一次修改都会变成服务器上的永久记录。戈夫曼说的后台消失、埃德蒙森担心的沉默、根特纳指出的“看不见废稿”，背后其实有同一个技术病根：**物理空间默认“阅后即焚”，而数字工具默认“永久留痕”。**当聊天记录随时可能被截图、检索或变成考评证据时，打工人本能的选择就是永远端着、只发定稿、绝不认错。对普通人而言，远程心累的真凶往往不是物理距离，而是“万物皆呈堂证供”的监控感；不切掉留痕压力，开再多线上茶话会也只是加班演戏。
summaries.advice: 结合全场智慧与“去留痕化”，这周就能上手三件事：第一，**给半成品和分歧建立“无痕通道”**——落实戈夫曼与哈森的建议，遇到坏消息、争议或拿不准的想法，立刻停止在群里打字留痕，改打一通不开摄像头、不录音的十分钟语音电话。第二，借根特纳与庄子“同作一器”的思路，带新人或自学时推行“废稿对照”：每周共享屏幕二十分钟，并排展示被毙掉的初稿和定稿，边改边讲差在哪，代替干瘪的汇报会。第三，照搬埃德蒙森与纽波特的动作：开会结尾点名问一位同事“这方案哪块最让你担心”，平时每天划出两段一小时的免打扰时间专注干活。
summaries.summary_en: A physical room never automatically created a team; it simply bundled trust, shared context, observational learning, and psychological safety together as free byproducts of proximity. Take away the room, and the team doesn't vanish, **but everything that used to happen by accident in shared air must now be deliberately designed and paid for—especially the hidden cost of training newcomers.** The real divide lies in how to rebuild it. Newport champions asynchronous rules and public boards to kill noise, while Edmondson, Goffman, and Hasson argue that workflows aren't enough—you must restore the safety to admit mistakes, an unscripted 'backstage,' and the warmth of the human voice. Zhuangzi and Huineng go further, questioning the obsession with constant contact itself: instead of exhausting each other with endless check-ins, true teams master their craft independently, build real things together, and meet with undivided presence only when it counts.
summaries.insight_en: Say something clumsy or sigh in an office, and the sound waves vanish into thin air; do it on remote platforms, and every word becomes a permanent record on a server. Goffman's missing backstage, Edmondson's invisible silence, and Gentner's vanished rough drafts all share a single technological root: **physical spaces are ephemeral by default, whereas digital tools are permanent archives by default.** When chat logs and video calls can be searched, screenshotted, or forwarded to management, workers naturally protect themselves by staying on-script, hiding messy drafts, and never admitting fault. For ordinary people, this means the real source of remote exhaustion isn't geographic distance, but the pressure of working inside an audit trail. Unless you carve out spaces free from permanent records, adding more virtual socials just means working overtime as an actor.
summaries.advice_en: Combining the panel's wisdom with the need for ephemerality, try three things this week. First, **create an 'off-the-record channel' for messy issues**—following Goffman and Hasson, whenever you hit a disagreement, bad news, or a half-baked idea, stop typing in public chats and jump on an unrecorded, camera-off audio call for ten minutes. Second, apply Gentner's comparison method and Zhuangzi's 'co-making': once a week, do a 20-minute live screen-share showing a rejected rough draft right next to the final version to explain the difference, replacing stiff status meetings with hands-on work. Third, pair Edmondson's and Newport's habits: end meetings by asking one specific teammate, 'What worries you most about this plan?' and block out two daily one-hour windows with notifications off to actually get deep work done.

hooks.text: **半屋子最难**：一半人在会议室、一半在屏幕上，屋里的人散会后在走廊拍板，远程的人只拿到结论。『一人远程、全员上线』够不够？混合办公是否注定分出二等成员？
hooks.text_en: **Half a room is the hardest**: half the team in the meeting room, half on a screen; the people in the room decide things in the corridor afterwards, and the remote ones get only the conclusion. Is 'one remote, all online' enough, or does hybrid work inevitably create second-class members?

hooks.text: **把消息写成一封信**：书信共和国的学者隔着几周的邮路照样合作，靠的是每封信都写得完整。远程团队能不能把『随发随问』改成『一次写清』？代价是谁多花时间？
hooks.text_en: **Write the message as a letter**: scholars in the Republic of Letters collaborated across weeks of postal delay because every letter was written to be complete. Can remote teams trade 'send now, ask later' for 'write it out once'? And who pays for that in extra time?

hooks.text: **谁来付带新人的账**：坐得近，新人得到的反馈多，老手的产出少。远程把这笔成本推给了谁？如果公司都只招熟手，下一代熟手从哪里来？
hooks.text_en: **Who pays for training newcomers?** Sitting close means more feedback for juniors and less output from seniors. Who does remote work push that cost onto? And if every company hires only the experienced, where does the next generation of experienced people come from?

hooks.text: **远程新人怎么补样本**：旁听不到前辈怎么回客户、怎么改稿，新人还能从哪里攒到足够的对照案例？
hooks.text_en: **How can a remote newcomer make up the missing cases?** If you can't overhear how seniors answer clients or revise drafts, where else can you collect enough contrasting cases?

answer.lead: 旁听的样本少了，就**主动去要对照**。按情境对照着补：

head: 情境
做什么
为什么
rows: 入职头三个月
争取每周至少一两天和带你的人同处一室
这时样本最缺，旁听的回报最高
只看得到定稿
请前辈给你看一份废稿，问他改了哪三处
成品藏起了判断，废稿才露出判断
学写邮件、方案
每次找两份同类的并排看，写下异同
并排比较能让结构从表象里浮出来
复盘会
要求同时摆出一个成了、一个砸了的方案
没有对照，结论记不住也用不上
不懂又不好意思问
在公开频道问，而不是私聊
答案留下来，下一个新人也能翻到
前辈太忙
约每月一次固定的一对一，提前写好三个问题
把偶然的点拨变成有准备的『入室』

answer.tail: 原则：**要对照，不只要范例**；要过程，不只要结论；问题留在公开处，让学习可以检索。

answer_en.lead: With fewer cases to overhear, **go out and ask for contrasts**. Fill the gap by situation:

head: Situation
What to do
Why
rows: First three months in the job
Push for at least a day or two a week in the same room as your mentor
That's when your stock of cases is thinnest and overhearing pays most
You only ever see final versions
Ask a senior for a discarded draft and which three things they changed
The finished product hides the judgment; the draft reveals it
Learning to write emails or proposals
Each time, put two of the same kind side by side and write down how they differ
Side-by-side comparison lifts the structure out of the surface
Post-mortems
Ask for one approach that worked and one that flopped, laid out together
Without contrast, conclusions neither stick nor transfer
You don't understand and feel awkward asking
Ask in the public channel, not a private message
The answer stays put, and the next newcomer can find it
Seniors are too busy
Book a fixed monthly one-to-one and write three questions in advance
It turns chance pointers into a prepared 'entering the room'

answer_en.tail: Principles: **ask for contrasts, not just examples**; ask for process, not just conclusions; keep questions in public so learning stays searchable.

hooks.text: **后台能设计出来吗**：闲聊群里一旦有领导，是不是立刻又成了前台？聊天软件把每句话都存档，说错一句就可能被截图——不留记录、不开摄像头，能不能人为造出一块真正的后台？
hooks.text_en: **Can a backstage be designed?** The moment a boss joins the chat group, does it turn straight back into front stage? Chat software archives every word, and one careless line can be screenshotted. With no records and no cameras, can you deliberately create a real backstage?

hooks.text: **跨时区：连节拍都没有**：同一时区还能打个电话，相差十二小时的团队几乎没有同步的时刻。只靠文字和录屏，共享背景还攒得起来吗？
hooks.text_en: **Across time zones, there's no rhythm at all**: within one time zone you can still pick up the phone, but a team twelve hours apart has almost no shared moments. With only text and recorded videos, can shared background still build up?

hooks.text: **同作一器，还是入室一谈**：庄子说手艺要两人一起动手，慧能说要一对一当面点破。说不出来的东西，到底靠并肩干活传，还是靠全心对坐的那一刻传？
hooks.text_en: **Make something together, or talk in the inner room?** Zhuangzi says craft passes when two people work on it together; Huineng says it passes when a teacher sets you right face to face. Is what can't be said handed on by working shoulder to shoulder, or in a moment of full attention across the table?
